title: FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) Assessment

questions.text: I fear others have more rewarding experiences than me
I fear my friends have more rewarding experiences than me
I get worried when I find out my friends are having fun without me
I get anxious when I don't know what my friends are up to
It is important that I understand my friends' inside jokes

sharedOptions: Not at all true of me

low.label: Low FOMO
low.description: You have a healthy relationship with social connection and missing out. You're comfortable with your own choices and don't feel excessively anxious about what others are doing. You can enjoy your own path without constant comparison.
steps: Keep doing what you're doing — your relationship with social media and social life is balanced
Continue practicing intentional presence in your daily activities
Maintain your healthy boundaries around phone usage and social commitments

moderate.label: Moderate FOMO
moderate.description: You experience FOMO at a noticeable level. Social media and peer comparisons occasionally make you feel like you're falling behind or missing important experiences. This level can start affecting your focus, self-esteem, and study habits if not addressed.
steps: Set specific social media time limits (try 30 min/day max) and stick to them
Practice the 'JOMO' (Joy of Missing Out) — intentionally skip one event per week and enjoy the downtime
Before checking your phone, ask: 'What am I avoiding right now?' — awareness breaks the habit
Unfollow or mute accounts that consistently trigger comparison
Keep a gratitude journal — write 3 things you're grateful for each evening
Remind yourself: social media shows highlights, not reality. You're comparing your behind-the-scenes to their showreel

high.label: High FOMO
high.description: You experience significant FOMO that is likely affecting your mental health, focus, and ability to study effectively. The constant worry about what others are doing steals your attention from the present moment and your own growth. This is very common in today's hyper-connected world — but it can be changed.
steps: Digital detox: Try one full day per week with no social media (start with 4 hours if a full day feels impossible)
Turn OFF all non-essential notifications. Your phone is controlling your attention — take it back
Practice 'delayed checking' — when you feel the urge to check your phone, wait 10 minutes. The urge will pass
Replace scrolling time with ONE meaningful activity (reading, walking, creating, exercising)
Have honest conversations with close friends about how social media makes you feel
Write down your own goals and values. When you're clear on YOUR path, others' paths matter less
Remember: every minute spent worrying about others' lives is a minute stolen from building your own
Consider speaking to a counselor — FOMO at high levels can be connected to anxiety that benefits from professional support
Practice mindfulness: spend 5 minutes daily just noticing your breath. This trains your brain to be present
Set 'phone-free zones': bedroom, study desk, and meal times. Protect these spaces
